panes.label: Ledger
panes.title: Retrieve a decision and prove it
panes.note: This is the examiner's question: explain the decision you made on this applicant months ago, and prove it has not been altered since. Retrieval walks the hash chain from genesis, loads the exact model version the decision was pinned to, and re-scores the stored application. Agreement to the last bit is the claim.

panes.label: Fairness
panes.title: Three questions, asked separately
panes.note: Raw approval-rate disparity, disparity that survives controls, and how much a protected characteristic can be reconstructed from the features themselves. They are different questions with different answers, and collapsing them into one fairness score loses the distinction that matters to a regulator.
panes.html:

7a · Raw approval rate disparity

What the four-fifths rule is, and is not The four-fifths rule is a screening heuristic drawn from the EEOC Uniform Guidelines on employee selection. It is not the legal standard for credit discrimination and a ratio above 0.80 does not establish compliance. It is reported as a first screen only; the controlled analysis is the substantive one.

7b · Disparity surviving controls

On controlling for geography Two specifications are reported because the choice is contested. County fixed effects control for genuine local economic variation, and they also absorb geographic discrimination, which is itself a fair lending concern. Neither is presented as the single correct answer.

7c · Proxy scan

How much each feature reveals about a protected attribute. Excluding race from a model does not remove it if another feature carries the same information.

Calibration The flag threshold (0.03) is a calibrated heuristic, not a natural constant: NMI magnitudes depend on sample size and binning. It is set so that a known geographic proxy is flagged while ordinary credit features are not. The negative control scores 0.0008, which is the floor this scan can resolve; each feature's multiple of that floor is reported so the calibration can be judged directly rather than taken on trust.
Joint predictability The model's feature set predicts an applicant's race and ethnicity group with macro-averaged AUC 0.735. An AUC of 0.5 would mean the features carry no information about group membership. This captures joint proxying — combinations of features that together identify a group even when no single feature does — which the pairwise scan cannot see.

8 · Less discriminatory alternative search

Under disparate impact doctrine a business-justified model remains challengeable if a comparably effective, less discriminatory alternative exists. This search covers a bounded hypothesis space; the absence of a better alternative within it is not proof that none exists.

A model with 1.1% lower AUC achieves 51% lower controlled disparity.

panes.label: Portfolio
panes.title: The same guarantees in bulk
panes.note: A portfolio run scores through the identical path — every row explained, every row recorded — and then re-runs the fairness analyses on what was actually decided rather than on a sample.
panes.html:
Pane 5

Portfolio review

Score a book of business, not one application. Every row lands in the decision ledger as a single chained batch with one receipt hash, and the same three fairness analyses run against that batch rather than against the static evaluation frame. This is the quarterly review a fair lending team actually performs.

panes.label: Validation pack
panes.title: The document writes itself
panes.note: Nothing in the pack is typed by hand. It is assembled from the artifacts the commands produced, which is why it can be regenerated whenever the model changes instead of being rewritten.
panes.html:
Pane 4

Generate the validation pack

A twelve-section model validation document, structured against the validation pillars of SR 11-7 and the technical documentation content of EU AI Act Annex IV. Every figure in it is read from a generated artifact; none is written by hand. Retrain the model and regenerate, and the document describes the new model with no editing.

Model validation pack

Reads the model registry, performance metrics, fairness report, alternative search, and drift report, then renders to PDF.
